What's the most fulfilled you've ever been at work? Does that fulfillment fall within your current job?

When I was in the military. Not because of political BS, or patriotism (although I am patriotic), but because of the friends I had. I wasn't in a combat role, per se. But I still would have taken a bullet for several of those guys and gals, even some of the ones I didn't really like. The ones I did like, I still would, and it's been 19 years since I got out.
Damn, the military never sounds like an easy job or one that should be undertaken lightly, but that sounds like the kind of fulfillment a lot of people go their whole lives searching for.

You're right. Even though I was never a front line guy, it wasn't easy. It was demanding work, especially for a bunch of really young people that are still trying to figure their shit out. I've never been in an environment that was as fun or as close knit. And it's bummed me out at every job I've worked at since.

I got a part-time research assistant job when I was in university and enjoyed it. After I graduated I tried my hand at a corporate job in a consulting firm for a year and I was miserable. This year I was offered a full-time role at the institute that gave me the RAship and it's been the best job ever. I learn a lot, the job is flexible, my bosses are great and I do fun and challenging work that's meaningful. More importantly I'm no longer feeling like I rip clients off, as I did at my old job but that I actually help inform people. Another plus point is I rarely feel emotionally stressed, but intellectually stressed instead - sometimes the work is hard and its stressful, but I know it'll make me better, compared to my old job where I was just often stressed with people. I don't earn as much as I would in a corporate job but I wouldn't trade it for the world.

That's why I want to get into research. Working for corporations is horrible from what I've heard, but my experience with research has been excellent. Great people to work with, great working conditions, you give a shit about your job, and knowing that you're making a positive difference in the world is wonderful. If I can't get into research, I'm still going to put off getting a real job for as long as possible.
Good luck! I have to say the nature of research funding makes it difficult to get straight into right after graduating, hence my corporate stint, but I really hope you make it!
That sounds pretty incredible! It's nice to hear that you found something meaningful where you don't feel like you're constantly lying to get ahead like most corporate jobs require.

Right now I'm more satisfied and happy in my job than I had ever imagined possible.

I've worked some cool jobs before. Game designer. Running a start up. Consultant. Teacher. Writer.

Today I'm a distiller.

I go to sleep without stress, and wake up early looking forward to going to work. I sit in front of a still, make great hooch and enjoy the hell out of my life. Good times.

That seems like the most attractive quality in a job for me - being able to go to sleep without stress and essentially leaving work at work. It sounds like you've had your share of careers. I'm glad you've found one you really enjoy!

A simple Azir wall trick. I'm not sure if people know about this yet

In case it's not clear in the video, you must meet your soldier in the wall. Since the game can't just leave you there, it will throw you out of it. A few spots will throw you very far, but it's hard to show where as they don't really make sense, but they ARE consistent. If you want to learn how to do it, just go into a custom and try to replicate what I did while watching the slow motion video. Once you get it a few times you will get a good feel for where you need to be. Bad ping makes things more difficult.

And yes, this is what is actually happening. In some cases you will "slide" instead of blink. If you slide, it did not work and you are not seeing what other people see. When coming out of a slide you cannot change walking direction, when coming out of successful blink you can immediately walk a different direction. I didn't in the video, but it can make for some nice escapes.
